newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, heating oil under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, heating oil under pressure.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Tuesday.
The Med gasoline market split firmly into two tiers with a firm higher octane market but a sloppy market for lower RON material.
Lower RON material cam under pressure from good supplies but poor demand from the eastern Mediterranean and West Africa.
Naphtha was supported by the closure of Algeria's Skikda terminal for nearly a week, which has already delayed three naphtha cargo liftings. The port is due to reopen tonight.
Cargoes were pegged at around cif quotes high +$4 cif Med.
Gas oil was slightly weaker. Heating oil came under pressure from lengthy Russian supplies, several offers of U.S. cargoes, and a potential arbitrage from the Red Sea, traders said.

Heating oil cargoes were still on offer at Nov IPE +$6.00 cif Med, without attracting much interest, and a diesel cargo was offered at Nov +$26 cif Med, although this market was thin. One trader said the Mediterranean was "grossly overvalued", but others said he was merely trying to depress prices temporarily in order to cover requirements into Greece or Turkey.
Traders reported the first signs of buying for Greece's 940,000-tonne October-March tender and for Turkey's 75,000-tonne October tender which closed on Tuesday.
Tight supplies of fuel oil continue to underpin firm prices. An ISAB cargo was sold by a trader to a trader at quotes high fob Med +$1 on Oct 27-31 dates.
A requirement to cover a 20,000-25,000-tonne tender cargo into Tunisia gave support and dealers said the market was already talking November barrels.
Traders were also talking about possible deals into Romania which is looking for 500,000 tonnes of fuel oil this winter.
